reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction from Sundar Pichai in 2019 that passes all four tests, so I've marked this a quiet year. All three fixed searches ran once each. They only turned up coverage from 2023 onward and secondary write-ups, nothing he said in 2019.

The one solid 2019 source is his October 23 question-and-answer interview with MIT Technology Review, about Google's quantum computing result. It has timed predictions, but none of them is about AI:
- **Quantum:** asked how far off something like improving the Haber process is, he said "I would think a decade away." That is about quantum computing.
- **Rules and ethics:** "over the next 10 years, we have to engage and work together on all of this." That is about working together on rules, not about what AI will do.
- **Health care (closest miss):** "In health care, I think we are on the verge of breakthroughs over the next decade or so which will be profound." He was answering a question about technologies other than quantum, and the sentence names health care, not AI. His next sentence is about AI but gives no date. I left it out as not clearly about AI; you may want to judge it yourself.

In the same interview he said both AI and quantum "are in early phases" and mentioned people who confuse AI with general artificial intelligence. Neither line gives a timeline for AGI, so the undated list is empty.

A few sources I couldn't use:
- **CNN's June 2019 "Boss Files" interview:** both CNN pages wouldn't open, so I quote nothing from it.
- **Fast Company's 2019 profile:** only partly loaded (it looks paywalled), and the part I saw had no prediction from him.
- **Google I/O keynote (May 7, 2019):** the transcript cut off partway through. In the part I read, his AI remarks gave no dates; the one "later this year" AI line came from Scott Huffman, another Google executive.

I used 11 of 12 searches. Search 1 went through but my code failed to print it, so I read its saved results rather than run it again. Five of the six page openings were used.
